Used to be that all you needed to steal a car in a GTA game was a few seconds and a sharp elbow. In GTA 6, you can still smash a window and hotwire some cars, but the car stealing system has changed a lot and the further you get into the game, the more tools you'll need.

That means a quick getaway in a stolen vehicle isn't always that simple. Here are the methods for stealing cars, the new tools you'll get and when they become available in the story, and everything else you need to know about boosting rides in GTA 6.

Want to steal a car? Walk up to the door and press the interact button. That'll tell you if it's locked (most are), if it's alarmed (nearly all are), and if it's keyless—a new type of car that we'll cover more below.

If you smash the window, you'll then climb into the car and need to hotwire it, which just takes a second or two and uses the control sticks to find the "sweet spot." If it's a keyless car, you won't be able to hotwire it or drive it away—again, more on that below. If you smash a window on an alarmed car, the alarm will sound, which can attract attention.

You can still pull people out of their cars, but be warned: many of them will fight back, meaning you'll need to hammer a button quickly to defeat them. Lose, and they'll clonk your head against the side of the car, knocking you down and speeding away. And even if you do pull them out of their car, this is Leonida: a lot of motorists are armed and aren't shy about opening fire.

You can't slim jim a car someone is already sitting in, so you'll have to break the window if the door is locked. Plus, there are car trackers to worry about now: more on that below.

In Chapter 1, in the sixth story mission called Unwanted Attention, your buddy Cal will help you install the "Waink It" app on your phone, which lets you scan cars to see their make and model, if they're locked, alarmed, keyless, or have trackers. The app will also tell you the condition of the car, how much it can be sold for, and what it costs to register them—registering stolen cars at Pay 'n' Spray shops is how you take ownership of them in GTA 6.

Want to get into a locked car without breaking the window or setting off the alarm? You'll need a slim jim, a tool that lets you pop the lock and open the door quietly.

You'll get this new tool in Chapter 2 of the main story, in the fifth mission called "Moses," where you meet an auto mechanic (Moses!) who will give you a slim jim and teach you how to use it. Now when you sidle up to a car door, you'll be able to use the slim jim to pop the lock: no broken windows, no alarms—though it takes a little longer than using your elbow. Again, you still won't be able to start keyless cars, even if you have a slim jim.

Here's the big one. Keyless cars can't be hotwired, so you'll need a key cloner. You'll get the key cloner in Chapter 3, in the 16th mission called "Steal the Zorruso for Randy." That's a long time to wait, but now you can stand next to the door of a keyless car and use your phone to clone its key.

Bonus: the key cloner will not only unlock the door but automatically start the car. That makes it worth the wait! However, keyless cars often come with another new system: trackers.

Not a big deal, really: if a car has a standard tracker, it just means you can't modify it at a mod shop unless you've paid to register the car as your own. I probably wouldn't modify a car unless I owned it anyway, so I never worried about standard trackers at all.

These can be a problem. Advanced trackers will notify the police that the car has been stolen and pinpoint your location—and the cops will respond quickly. To defeat the advanced tracker, you need to drive fast enough that the tracker won't be able to send a signal to the cops. Slow down, and it'll start beeping and you'll only have a few seconds to speed up again. If you fail to speed up enough, the tracker will pinpoint your location and the cops will be on you again.

You have to drive pretty fast to keep the advanced tracker from triggering, which makes it tougher to get them to a Pay 'n' Spray or a Randy's garage without doing some serious damage to the car. Good luck!

You can sell stolen cars at a Pay 'n' Spray, though there's a limit of three cars per day. You can also sell to your two automobile fences, Moses and Randy, though Moses only buys older model, low-end cars and Randy only buys certain flashy, expensive cars. Your Waink It app will tell you if a car is suitable for sale to either of them.

You can also store stolen cars at a garage if you've purchased one through the real estate app on your phone. Each garage only has room for a single car. You can also use a parking spot or spots outside your current safehouse to store a stolen car.

#3624. PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:

Rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take."

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

#3622. Wow, GTA 6 Has Some Incredible Animations

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar GamesTiny Details

Grand Theft Auto 6, out now on Xbox and PS5, is a very big game. But don’t assume it’s just a blandly massive world with no tiny details to discover. Rockstar Games has packed GTA 6 with more detail than any of its previous games, including some truly impressive animations.

Let’s start with one of the earliest animations I spotted that truly made me go “Whhhooooaaa…” I parked too close to a car, and Jason was unable to fully open his door. In past GTA games, this would lead to the character teleporting out of the car or the door clipping through the other vehicle. In GTA 6, that’s not the case. Instead, Rockstar has added a dedicated animation for Jason and Lucia where they squeeze in and out of the car.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is filled with tiny animations like this that often made me shake my head and think, “I guess I get why this took so long to make.” For example, there are so many animations connected to eating and drinking in this game. I mean, you can crack open a cold one with one hand while holding and shooting an assault rifle in the other.

I also discovered that Jason and Lucia can eat a burger while holding a soda at the same time and even switch between them whenever. And when your drink is empty, you can toss it in a nearby trash can with a procedural animation that doesn’t always work. I’ve missed the trash before, and I felt like an asshole. Jason and Lucia might be murderers who rob and steal, but they aren’t litterbugs!

One animation that really caught me off-guard happened when I was testing how much damage cars in GTA 6 can take before they stop working. I found an empty parking lot, lined up my car with a nearby wall, and floored the accelerator. I expected to slam into the wall and total the front of my vehicle. Instead…

Again, GTA 6 has so many surprising animations and details. I can’t list them all here because I know I’ve not found them all yet. Maybe I never will? Regardless, I highly recommend you poke around GTA 6 and try stuff out because you’re likely to find some wild detail or tiny animation you’ve never seen before.

And for those who want to see a few more, here’s a video compilation I put together of some tiny animations I spotted while playing GTA 6 over the last few weeks. No spoilers are included in the video below.

We’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious. This has not been the best season of The Traitors. In fact, you could easily say this has been a below-average season. Fans on social media and those I have talked to in real life seem to all be in agreement on that. There’s a growing consensus that the show needs to change. I think producers are going to listen, though I’m terrified they’re going to misunderstand the why.

The biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities. The US version of The Traitors has historically relied on reality television personalities to provide the drama and bring their fanbases. This season, NBC decided to move the property from Peacock to network television and cast it like a more traditional competition show with randoms. It would be easy to just look at that decision and blame all the problems on the newbies, but that’s actually not the right takeaway.

The biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes. The show simply does not work in an hour-long time slot on NBC. In theory, the episodes on Peacock are the same length, as they’re typically between an hour and an hour and ten minutes. Because they’re on streaming, however, that runtime is the actual length of each episode. On network television, an hour-long time slot is actually forty-two minutes or so of real content, which isn’t even close to the amount of time the players need to complete one cycle of the game.

That means every single episode, the editors are making an impossible choice. They can either not include one or more major elements of the show (the breakfast, the mission, the roundtable and the turret), they can completely remove all of the strategy scenes that happen between those major elements, or they can drop most of the confessionals where the players talk directly to the camera and tell us their motivations and theories. There is simply no way to get through all of that in forty-two minutes. So, that has left every episode feeling either incomplete because it didn’t make it through a full cycle of the game, or feeling like a highlight video that simply recaps the basics of what happened.

That format and structure are the problem. The runtime is the problem. It’s not the cast. Even with less confessionals and less screentime, we’ve gotten good content from these players. I’m not saying the Traitors: New Blood cast is better than the cast on Big Brother 14 or Survivor: Heroes vs Villains, but there are some breakout personalities here and plenty of likeable, solid characters who have popped and would have looked even better with more of a chance to talk to the camera.

Victor is an all-time great Traitors character and should be a reality television mainstay moving forward. He’s electric. I’m personally obsessed with Jay and have had probably ten conversations with people trying to figure out his vibe and what’s going on in his head. It’s not just those two standouts either. There are a half dozen or so other players who play hard and are capable of delivering strong confessionals. Joe, Katie, Tomica, Michael and Shane have all had great moments, and when given a chance, secondary characters like Wyatt, Clyde, Abby, Abbey, Kriste, Ben, Morgan and others have delivered too. They’re just not always getting the screentime because, once again, every episode feels like it’s set on 1.5X speed.

Survivor and The Amazing Race have lengthened their episodes in recent years to help develop the characters and let the episodes breathe more. That’s the obvious solution here for The Traitors. It either needs to move to 90 minutes, or it needs to move back to Peacock. What it absolutely does not need to do is give up on casting newbies. The UK and other countries have had fantastic seasons using randoms, and in an ideal world, it would be a delight to watch Peacock/ NBC switch back and forth between a season with reality stars and a season with plumbers, farmers and firefighters.

I love The Traitors. It’s one of my favorite shows on television, and despite the obvious format issues, I still enjoyed the content we got this season. I’d like to see producers listen to the fan frustration and make a change, but those alterations should be exclusively focused on the format and not on casting.

#3620. Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other big productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity."

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

The slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again."

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to New Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

#3618. GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

#3617. How Long Is GTA 6? Depends On How You Play

As I prepare to pick up and play Grand Theft Auto VI tonight, I’m bracing myself to be in Leonida pretty much non-stop for days, weeks, maybe even months. It just intuitivelyÂ feels like it’s going to be a doozy of a long game, huh?

After all its predecessor, GTA V, takes 32 hoursÂ just to rush through the main story (according to HowLongToBeat), and over 50 if you factor in side content. I’d expect its successor, especially with all the bells and whistles Rockstar is showing off, to take even longer.

With reviews out today, we now have a rough idea of what to expect, and yeah: this game’s gonna take time.

Our own reviewer, Zack, says he saw the credits roll at about 90 hours of gameplay. Granted, he was doing a lot of side content and wandering around and testing stuff, and not everyone will want to be anywhere near as thorough as he was. Zack suggests a speedier player might make it through in around 60 hours. Jeff Gerstmann, in his review, says he beat the game after about 45 hours, maybe 50 if you count some saves he had to reload throughout. Zack doesn’t think you can reasonably finish the story in much less than that.

For those looking for more to do, though, Zack has spent 150 hours in GTA VI and still hasn’t seen everything there is to see or done everything there is to do. Like past Rockstar games, GTA VI will let you keep playing after the credits roll (though in a slightly unusual way), so you’re free to turn Leonida inside out for days on end if that’s what you want to do.

Sorry to all the other games in my backlog, we might be here a while.

Did FBI plant the seeds for another spinoff?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for FBI Season 9, Episode 7, “Posterity,” streaming now with a Paramount+ subscription.

With FBI now in its ninth season on the 2026 TV schedule, the stakes have certainly been rising, and I’m not just talking about the professional ones. A show like FBI not only digs into the work aspect of the characters but the personal lives as well, even if it’s not shown as much. This week’s episode had a particularly surprising personal update for one of the characters, and that made me realize I had to ask the stars about spinoff potential.

Shantel VanSanten returned to FBI as Special Agent Nina Chase in Monday’s episode, “Posterity,” which marked her second appearance on the series since FBI: Most Wanted’s cancellation in 2025. Her return came just a couple of weeks after it was revealed that Nina had been offered a job to lead her own task force in San Diego, leading Scola (John Boyd) to question the logistics of their relationship and raising their son, Dougie. As Nina continued to pack and get in one last case at 26 Fed, Scola was still wrestling with how they were going to make things work. Ultimately, he told Nina he was going to put in a transfer and follow her to San Diego, meaning another FBI exit could be looming.

As Scola pointed out, though, it will still probably be a while until the transfer goes through. However, with him eventually moving out to California and Scolina taking the FBI by storm down there, this has spinoff potential written all over it. It would be fun to follow Scola and Nina in San Diego as Nina led her own task force, but would it ever happen? VanSanten and Boyd gave their take to CinemaBlend and, hilariously, have their own opinions on the ordeal:

FBI has been growing as a franchise, like any Dick Wolf series, so it’s totally logical to wonder about a spinoff coming from this update. Having two fan-favorite characters moving across the country for the job would certainly be a missed opportunity for another series, in my humble opinion. While it sounds like there aren’t any plans, and Boyd seems to be sticking around on FBI for the time being, if VanSanten has her way, we very well could be getting a Scolina spinoff at some point in the future. While we wait and hope for that, I'm just glad that it seems like Nina is finally getting closure.

As for what could happen in a potential Scolina spinoff, well, the possibilities are endless. Nina leading her own task force and seeing how she evolves in that leadership position would definitely be a great focus point. Scola would probably be settling into a new FBI field office, but the two of them would still stick to their deal of not going on cases together. We’d also probably get more of them and Dougie, who we definitely have not seen enough of. The story is there, and so are the characters, and I would love it if it happened. But if not, I’d hope that Boyd isn’t leaving FBI any time soon.

Now, for the time being, Scola will continue working out of 26 Fed. Considering all the cast changes that FBI has been through in recent years, I’m hoping that Boyd doesn’t leave the series any time soon, no matter how much I want a Scolina spinoff. Nina may be moving, but fans can still see Scola and co. in new episodes of FBI on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

But there’s a lot of head-scratching going on at the games nominated for Best Fighting Game, shining an uncomfortable light on how anemic the genre has gotten outside of the big twoâTekken and Street Fighter.

Nominated for Best Fighting Game 2026 are Marvel TÅkon: Fighting Souls, Invincible Vs, 2XKO, Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, and My Hero Academia: All’s Justice.

Woof. Let’s break down these nominees. 2XKO is dead, with active development ending on the game at the end of December, a few short weeks after the Game Awards take place. Invincible Vs has had its development team busted down to a “skeleton crew.” The Avatar Legends team features a developer accused of sexual harassment and is a part of the currently shrinking Paramount Games thanks to the Skydance merger. I’m not sure that many people even knew about All’s Justice, which feels like it was thrown in there to pad out the list.

It’s hard to make a fighting game viable. NetherRealm’s Mortal Kombat 1 earned favorable player sentiment when it was released in 2023, but the game fell off so hard in the years since that EVO 2026 marked the first time a NetherRealm game hadn’t been featured in the main event lineup since 2011. It seems like nearly every new fighting game fails either before or right after it launches. (Paging Multiversus.) Even Marvel TÅkon, which will almost assuredly win the category, seems to be facing an uphill sales and concurrent player battle to stay alive.

And yes, that’s true of 95 percent of games in this day and age, but fighting games are one of the genres particularly sensitive to that pressure. It’s almost miraculous that Keighley was even able to drum up enough games to flesh out the category at all. And I don’t know how much longer he’ll be able to do that for.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Even though Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking over the world tomorrow, World of Warcraft: Forever was the first game this month that people flocked to in record-breaking numbers.

While we don't know the exact player count like we do with games on Steam, we can make an educated guess on just how many people dove into the MMO via a recent set of statistics from Blizzard. According to the official WoW X account, over 15 million characters were created in the last few weeks.

Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. This is a game where you can put hundreds of hours into one character before ever reaching the level cap. There definitely aren't 15 million total players based on this statistic, but the number might not be massively below that.

I can't say I'm surprised that a spin-off MMO that will remain stuck in the most universally nostalgic era of WoW was a big hit. Everyone who stopped playing for one reason or another came back to remember what it was like to smack a scorpion for 38 seconds.

Whether or not they'll stick around is the question. Blizzard plans on updating the game with new things to do for players at different stages of the long leveling journey. Most people are still weeks away from reaching the level 60 cap, partially because there are so many things to do that don't involve XP. The first raid is around the corner, but I'm curious to see what kind of stuff is added for those of us who are still chilling in the mid-30s. It'd better be good because many of us will be on vacation in Leonida for the next several weeks.

#3613. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

#3612. Love Is Blind’s Sarah Reveals Where She Stands With Ex John Amid Divorce

Love Is Blind season 11 star Sarah Williams holds no grudges against her estranged husband, John Shannon, amid their ongoing divorce.

“I think I would say that we’re friends, but at a distance,” Sarah, 34, said on the Wednesday, November 18, episode of the “What’s the Reality” podcast. “I’m putting myself first.”

Sarah and John, 33, got engaged sight unseen on the latest season of Love Is Blind, which debuted on Netflix last month after filming in 2025. While the twosome were the only season 11 couple to get married, Sarah filed for divorce in June. John claimed during the tell-all reunion that their marriage ended after he made a “mistake” by exchanging explicit texts with a stripper. Sarah, however, later revealed that there were other reasons for her divorce petition, including losing self-confidence after John’s alleged mistreatment and name-calling.

John has since issued a public apology to Sarah, who has tried to maintain certain boundaries with her ex.

“The distance has been great, I will say,” she noted on Wednesday’s episode. “Now, when we do talk, I’m like, ‘No, no, we’re not talking about that [and] I’m not doing that.’ It gets easier and easier with time.”

Sarah continued, claiming, “He also hasn’t signed the [divorce] papers.”

When pressed by podcast host AD Smith about whether John is likely trying to “hold on to what little he has left” or “doesn’t want [the marriage] to be over,” Sarah speculated that may be the case.

“I think it’s a little bit of both,” she added. “I think he will now. … [The experiment is serious and] that’s the one thing I wish viewers would know is that, like, when you’re in it, it’s so serious.”

Sarah is now looking forward to her post-divorce chapter, though diving back into the dating scene is not on her agenda just yet.

“I’m going to take a little break from dating. I think I just need to get a clear head, remind myself of who I am,” she said. “And then, I don’t know. I don’t have any expectations. I’m like, ‘I just need a break.’”

Even so, Sarah remains hopeful to walk down the aisle again.

“Give me some time, [but] I think marriage is so great,” she noted. “You just have to find it, [but] it’s like, ‘Where?’”

Sarah further revealed that she’ll take the lessons from her failed marriage into future relationships.

“This was obviously, like, a crazy life learning experience for me. I don’t know how it would have been if I hadn’t said yes [at the altar],” she mused. “It was really hard. I’m grateful for the learning experience, but I wish we had just said, ‘Let’s try to date,’ and it would have gone differently. I would have left — and John knows this — I would have left fast.”

Love Is Blind is currently airing on Netflix.

It’s been a huge year for Robert Pattinson and Zendaya. The latter has already been in two of the biggest movies of the year, The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, while the former co-starred with Zendaya in The Odyssey and The Drama, and received praise for his role as Chris Hanson in Primetime. They are starring again in Dune: Part Three, which hits the 2026 movie schedule on December 18th (“DunesDay”). Pattinson, you may have heard, also landed the role of a lifetime yesterday when he was named the next James Bond.

The James Bond role may have come (indirectly) due to Zendaya introducing Pattinson to director Denis Villeneuve, who is not only at the helm of Dune, but upcoming, as-yet-untitled James Bond 26 as well. Last March, well before the Pattinson announcement, CinemaBlend attended an event featuring the premiere of the Dune: Part Three trailer followed by a Q&A with some of the cast, including Pattinson and Zendaya. The two had recently worked together on The Drama, and Pattinson talked about how he got involved with Dune, saying:

I absolutely adore these [Dune] movies. I saw them multiple times in theaters, and I think I was talking to you [Zendaya], on the set of The Drama and was like ‘Can I get in one of those Dune movies?

While Zendaya does acknowledge that she “knows a guy,” talking about Villeneuve, whom she worked with on the first two Dune movies, she doesn’t take full credit. However, Pattinson continues:

And it was a very unexpected call I got a few months later and I kind of did think you had something to do with it. I just think it's such a towering achievement, that the cast is so incredible. And, uh, I just think everybody wants to work with Denis, I mean, he’s just such a master.

You can see the whole answer from the Q&A here:

Sooo does Zendaya get credit for getting Robert Pattinson cast in "Dune 3" and James Bond now? The actor revealed earlier in 2026 how his "The Drama" costar introduced him to Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next 007 installment. https://t.co/3bBS1ydc8pNovember 16, 2026

Which brings us to James Bond. After working with Villeneuve on Dune: Part Three, Pattinson was obviously excited about working with the Canadian director again, and now he’ll get his chance in a big way. He’ll be stepping into massive shoes once filled by the likes of Sean Connery, Roger Moore, Pierce Brosnan, Daniel Craig, and all the other actors who have played Bond over the years.

The choice is not without some controversy, naturally, but speaking for myself, I’m excited. I always expected Amazon MGM, who now own the franchise, to go with a big star, and I think they’ve made a very solid choice with Pattinson, even though he’s only really dabbled in action movies. It takes a lot of layers to play a Bond well, and I think Pattinson has all the gears needed to pull it off.

This also leads to another obvious question: could Zendaya be the next “Bond Girl”? Before yesterday, she was a long shot on the prediction markets, but her odds have shot way up in the last 24 hours. She’s currently at 32% on Kalshi, sitting just behind the favorite, Margaret Qualley. I’m skeptical that she will be, but The Drama proved the two actors have great on-screen chemistry, so who knows? We’re all waiting for the announcement!

#3610. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

It's here. GTA 6 has been loosed upon the world, and another nation's productivity goes dark as each advancing hour unleashes midnight unlocks on the next timezone. And hey, from the sounds of it, people seem to like what they're finding—and they're finding a lot.

You can mini-golf. You can go on beach dates. You can text and drive (don't). You can doomscroll, and birdwatch, and ride a jetski with a dog. GTA 6 is dense with possible activities, actions, systems, and mechanics, but not everyone is having the best luck navigating the maelstrom of associated controls and button prompts. Allow me to present Japanese X user @Shunep3_STS, who on this day represents all of us:

操作が増えて覚えきれず、間違えて２つ買ったシェイクをしゃがみ歩きしながら飲み干すヤバい奴になってる https://t.co/OLXaEQGc7CNovember 18, 2026

"There are so many new controls I can’t keep them all straight," said @Shunep3_STS via machine translation, "and now I’m that guy chugging two shakes I accidentally bought while walking around in a squat."

There's something magical about this image. To begin with, the scene—like all of GTA 6—looks profoundly, almost grotesquely expensive: the delicate feathering of Jason's forearm hair, the pseudo-memoji of Cal in the text message notification, the fidelity of pebbled sand that probably cost more to realize in-game than I've spent on rent in the last three years. It's a tableau of technological excess.

And all of that's being deployed to present a man double-fisting slushies in an empty parking lot as he skulks like an imperiled raccoon. Look at him! Look at his face! He's got his chiseled jaw set like he's Solid Snake, but he's nursing a tummy full of iced corn syrup because the pilot controlling his body got too overwhelmed by which buttons do what.

And he's not alone: Our own Andrea Shearon is one of the many struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of button prompts in GTA 6. "There's so much going on," she said. "I just walk up to people and kind of mash all the face buttons for a surprise. You never know if I'm gonna punch someone or do squats or flip them off."

She's spent a lot of time accidentally making rude gestures at her snake as a result.

#3607. Rex Ryan Accused of Having ‘Small Penis’ by Pedestrians He Allegedly Ran Over

Former NFL coach Rex Ryan had his manhood challenged by a Nashville pedestrian he allegedly ran over with his truck.

“My wife and I both got ran over by some a**hole on f***ing Broadway,” a man said in a 911 call released by TMZ on Tuesday, November 17. “I want to turn him in.”

The man added, “He literally ran us over. Ran over my feet!”

When asked by the dispatcher to describe the vehicle in question, the man described it as a “big red pickup truck with oversized wheels that said ‘small penis.’”

The man insisted he and his wife didn’t need an ambulance, but said, “My toes are going to be a mess tomorrow.”

“We ran him down so I could get the license plate number,” the caller said, which he then relayed to the dispatcher.

The caller insisted about the driver, “He f***ing needs to be arrested.”

Ryan, 63, was arrested on November 11 after turning himself in to authorities at the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.

He was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failing to give information/render aid and two counts of failing to obey traffic signals.

Ryan was released after posting a $6,000 bond. He is due for a court hearing on December 18.

Michael Holland, the man allegedly struck by Ryan, claimed he and his wife were “almost killed” in the incident.

“If we had been six inches further out, I’d be in a hospital right now, and so would my wife,” Holland told the California Post in a story published on Friday, November 13.

Holland added, “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.”

When Holland and his wife tracked Ryan down, he claimed the former coach “got out and confronted us.”

“He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done,” Holland alleged. “Instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off.”

Holland said he was concerned that Ryan “was really going to hurt somebody.”

“I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” he said. “His tire literally was so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that.”

Landman is making quite the splash down in Texas right now, as people saw the show being filmed at a Texas Christian University game over the weekend. Then, not long after that, Ali Larter posted a photo dump from filming, and it featured one person I never expected to see: Glen Powell.

Of course, I’m well aware that Glen Powell is dating Michelle Randolph, Larter’s on-screen daughter and a veteran of Taylor Sheridan’s shows. He’s also famously from and lives in Texas, which is where Landman is filmed. So, it’s not illogical for him to be around the set of this popular Paramount+ show. However, I was still surprised to see him in the final slide of Larter’s photo dump. Take a look:

In that final slide, you can see Larter posing for a photo with her co-stars, Billy Bob Thornton and Michelle Randolph, as well as Glen Powell.

Now, Landman has actually been filming at Texas Christian University since October, per the university. However, it made headlines over the weekend because Randolph was spotted with the cheerleaders on Saturday during the game against the Kansas State Wildcats.

In Landman, she plays Ainsley Norris, the daughter of Thornton’s Tommy and Larter’s Angela. She’s a student at TCU, and a big part of her storyline has to do with her joining the cheer team. It would seem it will be an even bigger part of her arc in Season 3, seeing as not only was Randolph seen filming at this game, but Larter and Bobbi Salvör Menuez, who play Paigyn, were there too.

To top it all off, Glen Powell was also spotted at the game. As you can see in the third image of this carousel TCU uploaded, the Twisters actor was on the sidelines – which is also where his girlfriend happened to be.

A post shared by TCU (@texaschristianuniversity)

Rumors that Powell and Randolph were dating picked up in late 2025, and the actors went Instagram official in July of this year. Since then, they’ve posted pictures of each other here and there, and the Running Man star’s dog, Brisket, even made a cameo in one of the 1923 actress’s photo dumps.

Speaking of Brisket, Powell’s dog also gives him another tie to Landman. In early 2025, Brisket met up with Demi Moore’s pup, Pilaf. Man, it’s really a small world, and maybe I shouldn’t be shocked that he now has a connection to another star of this Taylor Sheridan show.

Overall, it was very cute to see the Top Gun: Maverick star pop up in a photo dump all about Landman. Clearly, he’s being a supportive partner and cheering Randolph on as she literally cheers on TCU. I also bet it’s pretty cool to just say you get to hang out with her, Ali Larter, Billy Bob Thornton, and Sam Elliott.

Now, I think the question becomes: Could we get Glen Powell on Landman? Taylor Sheridan has a tendency to hire A-listers for his shows, so I don’t think it’s out of the question. Plus, these images make it clear that the Chad Powers star is already literally very close to the production.

#3605. 32 Spoiler-Free Tips As You Hop Into Grand Theft Auto 6

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar GamesTips

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. The long wait was totally worth it. It is one of the best games I’ve played in many years and easily the best Grand Theft Auto game ever made. It is also a big, complicated, and deep game, with so much to do and see.

So, to help you out, here’s a bunch of tips for players hopping into GTA 6 this week. Don’t worry, no spoilers are included below.

Without spoiling anything, there are some incredibly big surprises and really memorable moments buried in this game. I highly recommend that people avoid watching too many videos about GTA 6 ahead of playing it to avoid ruining one particular late-game moment that might be one of my favorite video game surprises in years.

Before you rush out the door to do some missions or rob a liquor store, take a moment to grab a bite and a drink. These items will buff your health, stamina, and focus meter, letting you take more damage, run longer, and slow down time more during combat.

And hey, don’t assume that just because you’re drinking a soda or eating a hot dog, you have to stop moving or shooting. In GTA 6, you can move, shoot, run, hold hands, and even drive while holding and eating food. Finally, you can crack a cold one while shooting a rifle.

Around the map, you’ll encounter dogs and cats. If you hold the left trigger, you can zoom in on them and then praise and pet them. And you should do this, not just because dogs and cats are great, but also because it buffs your focus and rewards you with some good behavior points toward your criminal profile.

In GTA 6, you can store guns and clothes in your personal car’s trunk. And you should do this, as changing clothes is a great and fast way to lose the attention of the police.

You can manage your clothing, create new custom outfits, and store clothes in your trunk at any clothing store with a changing room, so don’t feel like you have to head back home to change your outfits around or remove stuff from your trunk. Just find a store.

Also, Rockstar lets you rename your custom outfits using a list of pre-existing words, like clubbing, hunting, or everyday. I recommend doing that to make it easier at a glance to see what everything stored in your trunk actually is without having to put it on and check.

When you go out shopping for clothesâand you will likely do that because dressing up is so much fun in this gameâbring both Jason and Lucia. This will let you buy clothing for both of them, try on new items as either character, and modify their current attire. And bonus: Buying clothing for your partner gets you some extra romance points.

The world of Leonida is packed with random events and moments that you can encounter while just walking around. These can be as simple as a drug deal going bad, or as complex as someone who needs help finding their missing spouse after a night partying. Often these events will be signaled to the player via shouting or other loud noises. If you hear something like that, click the left and right sticks to activate focus mode and find the source of the commotion, and then go investigate it.

I spent many hours making sure to close it first, then realized it closed when you drive away. You can also hold left on the D-pad to access your car’s features, including the ability to turn off headlights and close (or open) the trunk.

This section of Jason and Lucia’s phone will update as you play and will remind you to call certain characters or reply to texts. This can often reveal new story moments and dialogue between Lucia and Jason and their various friends and criminal cohorts.

Very early into GTA 6, you unlock the ability to explore underwater shipwrecks and find valuable loot. And you should do some of these in the early hours of GTA 6 to earn some easy cash. Plus, it’s just fun to explore the ocean.

On Jason and Lucia’s phones, you’ll find an app called Scooter Bros. This lets you manage your owned vehicles, spawn them near you, and even repair them. However, this isn’t free and early on money will be tight, so be careful how often you rely on this convenient app. It can also get vehicles out of police impound lots, but that ain’t cheap.

It costs $12,500 to upgrade to the premium version of the Scooter Bros service, which, for many hours in the game, is going to be more than you can spare. But once you feel comfortable spending that much, I recommend it. It gives you three free uses of the app every in-game day, which saves money in the long run. Plus, the app is upgraded and says you’re premium, and that’s nice.

Eventually, GTA 6 will let you buy garages around the map. These aren’t very useful while driving about, but they do give you more slots to store cars and motorcycles as you build up Jason and Lucia’s fleet of personal vehicles. Try to buy some when you can so you can have a wide array of customized bikes, cars, and trucks at your disposal.

You don’t have to, but if you want to do so, just tap left or right to signal to other drivers which way you are turning. In my testing, NPC drivers did seem to react to these signals. One more silly detail in GTA 6.Â

Jason and Lucia can both tag enemies while aiming at them with weapons or using binoculars. This will let you keep track of them and make sneaking around compounds much easier. Oh, and don’t forget to use focus to see enemies making noise and moving around, too.

Binocs can also be used to study the many, many animals in GTA 6 from a safe distance.

When sneaking into a place to rob it, use focus to spot which doors are connected to the alarm system quickly. These doors will glow red. Avoid kicking these doors in and work around them or lockpick them once you have that tool.

Zombix is the in-game medicine that you can pop during combat to heal up. You can find it in the world for free. But if you need some, you can also buy it at stores. Just talk to the clerk to buy some, as it’s often not stocked in the store like food and drinks.

Refueling cars is the main purpose of gas stations, but don’t forget you can also repair your car or motorcycle for a small fee at any gas pump, too. This is often cheaper than using the Scooter Bros app.

In GTA 6, you can hold down on the D-pad to slow down time and see nearby points of interest, missions, and other locations worth checking out. You can also mark any of these spots, and then the game will give you directions via the GPS. It’s faster than opening the map and useful for finding nearby gas stations if you’re running low on fuel.

If you steal a car and you spot a red tracking icon in the bottom left, near the engine and gas icons, you should probably get out quickly. That red icon indicates the car is fitted with an advanced tracker, and police will be able to find you on the map if you drive slowly for too long. You’ll want to avoid these cars until much later in the game when you get the ability to remove these trackers for a high cost. Use the Waink app on your phone by holding up on the D-pad to quickly scan cars and check for trackers.

In GTA 6, cops won’t always pull their guns out and try to arrest or shoot you. Instead, a one-star wanted level can be erased if you just talk to the cop and defuse the situation. Hold the left trigger to focus on the cop (make sure you don’t have a gun out), and you’ll see the option to defuse or provoke the cop. This works on any NPC and might let you avoid violence. Some people will still attack or harass regardless of whether you try to stay calm and defuse the situation, though.

While exploring the map, if you feel a sudden and intense vibration pulsing in your controller, stop and look around with the Waink app. There’s likely some art or something else worth scanning nearby.

Don’t be a litterbug. Giving a hoot boosts your focus and gives you some good behavior points.

While you’ll be able to find similar items and hairstyles at all stores and barber shops, most of these places also have exclusive options available only at that spot. So exploreÂ  and see what you can find.

If you just want a quick and simple trim, you can always look at your mirror in your safehouse bathroom and cut your hair down. You can’t change the style beyond that, though. I guess only the barbers and stylists in Vice City have the magic power to make hair grow back instantly.

Leonida is Rockstar’s digital recreation of Florida. And as someone who grew up in Florida, I was raised to always assume a gator is in every body of water. That’s a good rule of thumb when playing GTA 6, too.

While I encourage everyone to take their time (see next tip), if you really want to get somewhere fast, just use the RydeMe app to call a driver, and then once you’re in the car, hold the left trigger to focus on the driver and get the option to fast travel to your destination for $100.

Listen, how long have you already waited to play this game? Trust me, it’s worth slowing down and taking it all in. There’s so much to see, do, and discover out there, and most of it will pass you by if you speedrun the game.

If I can pinpoint one disappointing aspect of GTA 6 that most will agree on, it's the fact that it runs at 30 fps.

Many of us remember when this was normal for consoles (especially the PS3/Xbox 360 era), but these days, it's unusual for a major game to not offer a 60 fps or 40 fps performance option. Unfortunately, even if you're rocking a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 moves at a filmic 30.

That's disappointing news for anyone who shelled out $900+ for the more powerful PS5 Pro expecting better performance (or vindicating news, if you're a PC Gamer reader waiting for the arbitrarily delayed PC version), but Rockstar insists there was no way around it.

Speaking to Kotaku, technology production director Marc Chambers explained that the current consoles just aren't powerful enough to keep up without significant compromises.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," he said. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

Head of development Rob Nelson framed the decision to skip performance mode in much simpler terms to IGN:

"It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer," he said. "Too much, too much."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I don't actually have a problem playing a slow-paced game like GTA 6 at half the usual framerate so long as it's consistent and smooth, I can't deny that these quotes left me cracking a smile in the direction of my PC.

The world of Leonida does look unbelievably impressive at times—both in terms of pure graphical oomph and the density of vehicles, NPCs, and reactive foliage—but a great PC is going to demolish it. I've been searching for a game that will make this RTX 5090 actually flinch, and honestly, I'm doubtful even GTA 6 will be it. Barring a suite of PC-only enhancements that raise its requirements by a lot, I can't imagine a game that targets an Xbox Series S will have trouble blowing past 60 fps on top PC hardware.

This is putting into perspective for me that, while I wasn't looking, the current consoles got old. That's fine, to be clear—we're in the middle of a tech pause that has me happily playing older games anyway—but it's a wasted opportunity that GTA 6 is debuting exclusively on mid hardware.

We have to wait an unspecified amount of time to get what is destined to be the best version of this generational game. As Chris said in his writeup after 100 hours with GTA 6, "It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC."

#3603. Derek Hough Addresses Criticism Over His 'Dancing With the Stars' Judging

Derek Hough is weighing in on criticism surrounding his Dancing With the Stars judging as season 35 comes to an end.

“This season, there’s a lot going on. There’s the whole thing about me [giving out] the nines,” Hough, 41, exclusively told Us after the semifinals on Tuesday, November 17, referring to how he gave every routine the same score one week prior.

Despite the conversations online, Hough has remained unbothered.

“The reason why that doesn’t bother me at all is because I think anybody that knows me, if you’ve been to one of my shows, if you see me do what I do, if you see me host, if you see anything you see me do, it’s one thing I’ve always been,” he noted. “I consistently show up.”

The judge defended his choice to “come with 110 percent energy” at all times.

“You come to any of my shows, anybody can attest to that,” Hough added. “So I know that I give my absolute all no matter what. Do I sometimes have an off night? Sure, absolutely.”

Hough has been willing to accept feedback, adding, “I’m not exempt from imperfection. But one thing I do know about myself is, I show up. I show up no matter what and I’m a professional in what I do.”

After spending years as a DWTS pro — and winning six mirrorball trophies — Hough moved behind the judges table, offering his perspective on how the show has changed. “But I do feel like the energy around the show is a reflection of the popularity of the show, right? People are having conversations and things like that,” he said. “I would hope that moving forward, we can move toward more enjoyment and what people like about it versus what you don’t.”

He concluded: “Because I feel like what’s bad is always available. So is what’s good. And where our focus goes, our energy flows. So we want to put more energy and focus into what’s good, into each other, and into the show and into the world. There’s enough bad stuff out there. We don’t need to add more to it.”

In addition to judging on DWTS, Hough is also looking forward to the debut of his and wife Hayley Erbert‘s documentary, The Symphony of Dance, which follows the aftermath of her cranial hematoma. (She underwent emergency surgery in 2023 after a life-threatening brain bleed.)

“For us, it’s a beautiful piece of archival footage to have that just tells her story, tells her story really of resilience and overcoming something that was terrifying,” Hough noted. “But also it is a beautiful journey of returning to the stage, reclaiming a part of herself. That was incredible.”

Erbert, 32, admitted she was initially hesitant about the project. “I always say that I’m a private person living a public life, and so it’s a little interesting sharing something that’s so raw and so horrible,” she told Us. “But honestly, it was receiving messages after the fact when I’ve inspired somebody in some way, whether it was mentally, physically, emotionally. And after that, I was like, ‘You know what? If this can help one more person, then absolutely, I’m all for it.’”

Dancing With the Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET.

#3602. Zara Tindall Shows Cheltenham Why She's The Queen of Race Day Dressing

Zara Tindall didn’t let the cold snap stop her from enjoying a day at the races on Friday. Accompanied by her close friend Dolly Maude and country-set favorite fashion designer Jade Holland Cooper, the daughter of Princess Anne and granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II brought a dash of regal glamour to the proceedings following a glitzy night out in support of Prince William.

And while the sun may have been out, the Olympic equestrian still needed to wrap up against the chill. Tindall opted for a long plaid coat from L'Agence, a Purdey roll-neck jumper in brown, and a fascinator from Sally-Ann Provan. She accessorized with a new pair of Hector Lion earrings, a new Fairfax & Favor handbag, and completed the look with leather boots, also from Fairfax & Favor.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

Dolly, on the other hand, wore an avant-garde feather coat with knee-high boots and what looked to be a pair of emerald tights.

The pair were last spotted together in October, when they attended the William Hill Showcase Meeting at Cheltenham, but their friendship goes way back. Long considered Zara’s best friend, Dolly became Princess Anne’s lady-in-waiting in 2024. A former NHS midwife, she helped to deliver Zara’s third child, Lucas Tindall, on the floor of Zara’s bathroom at Gatcombe Park after the plan for the birth went awry in 2021.

Jade Holland Cooper and Zara Tindall on day one of The November Meeting at Cheltenham racecourse

But Dolly’s bond with the niece of King Charles III goes back long before that. (Not for nothing did Zara’s husband, Mike Tindall, joke that the 53-year-old is “more important than I am.”) Dolly was Zara’s maid of honor when the pair tied the knot, and when Zara split from her then-fiancé, jockey Richard Johnson, in 2003, the pair moved in together—they still live close by in the Cotswolds.

Having worked as a maternity practitioner in the NHS in Gloucestershire for 13 years, Dolly also did some philanthropic work using her maternity expertise, working in the unit of a hospital in Kambia, Sierra Leone for a month in 2013. At Kambia, she taught staff basic nursing skills. Before qualifying as a nurse, Dolly studied fashion and Cordon Bleu cookery at Eastbourne College of Food and Fashion, graduating in 1989.

Zara Tindall also braved the stormy weather for a day at Cheltenham with Dolly in October

Dolly Maude is known for her love of horses—a passion she shares with Zara and Princess Anne—and is often seen in Ascot’s royal box alongside the Princess Royal. In March 2024, she made her first official appearance as the Princess Royal’s lady-in-waiting, a momentous occasion that marked a new phase of her enduring bond with the royal family.

The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

Concerning Dolly’s appointment, another friend of Mrs. Maude's told The Telegraph, “She’s such a great girl. For the Princess Royal, it’s a perfect fit because of their shared love of dogs and horses. She’s not only extremely close to Zara, she also gets on brilliantly with the Princess. She’s fiercely loyal and discreet. It’s a great match.”

While much of Zara Tindall’s time this season has been spent touring the country’s most prestigious racing meets, she still found time to support her cousin, Prince William, at one of his treasured annual traditions. The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

Zara showcased her characteristically elegant style, donning a sapphire-blue Rebecca Vallance short-sleeved midi number, aptly named the “Crown Jewel” dress, which she paired with Kiki McDonough earrings. It is not the first time that the royal has lent her support to Prince William’s second-longest patronage: she also joined the crowd at the Tusk Awards in 2025, donning Rebecca Vallance again, and tearing up at the Prince of Wales’ speech in honor of those who gave their lives as rangers.

Zara Tindall and the Marchioness of Bath at the Tusk Awards

#3601. How Am I Supposed To Wait Until The PC Version To Play GTA 6?

I have no desire to be an iconoclast. Today’s launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is by far the biggest release in all of gaming history, and on pre-orders alone it’s already the biggest game of 2026. It’s the most expensive game ever made, and it seems inevitable that it’ll be the highest-grossing game ever released. Not only that, but it’s also extraordinarily good. It’s a pinnacle in gaming, and it’s going to be the focus of the worlds I exist in for months to come. Of course I want to be a part of this. But I also want to playÂ GTA 6 for the first time on PC.

I’ve always playedÂ GTA games on PC. Partly because I sometimes didn’t own the relevant PlayStation at the time, and partly because the first 20 years of my career were primarily spent covering PC games. But also because the PC versions were always better. That’s not some silly factional position, or dumb anti-console nonsense, but rather just a statement of fact. Rockstar would put out the console version, then spend six months removing all the artificial limitations and adding all the features that had remained stuck on wish lists, and then let the game loose into the unfettered technology of personal computing. The PC release is always the definitive version of any Grand Theft Auto, complete with six months of bug fixes on top of the myriad improvements, and what better way to first experience a great game than in its finest form?

Except, is that even realistic this time? Let’s entirely put aside the notion that as some manner of “games journalist,” it’s arguably important that I be culturally aware of the biggest game release ever. I’m also a person who wants to enjoy a game in the way he wants to enjoy it. But dear god, the pressure to play the moment my clock hits midnight. Heck, for me that’s five hours earlier than it is for folks in the U.S.! I’ll be ahead of the curve! And everyone else I know will be playing this game in every moment they can. The mimetic pressure alone is overwhelming.

This time I certainly do own the console, and although my PS5 doesn’t get a lot of use (here again I appear to have accidentally gone against the curve, but I just find my Xbox Series S and Game Pass to be a much more attractive prospect), it’s there and ready to offer me a game that a few of my colleagues have already finished and assure me I’m going to adore. And I want to be adoring it! Zack’s review is making this all the harder for me, as he so beautifully describes the minutiae of the game, the smallest details that seem so deeply attractive. I’m so astonished to learn that each of the two main characters has their own distinct social life, and can get up to their own business while you’re playing as the other. I want to experience that! And I can, in just 12 hours’ time. But…I want to experience it at its best, and I can’t for at least five more months.

I’m so torn! There’s absolutely no part of me that thinks it’s somehowÂ interesting to not play GTA 6. Ooh, look at me, the artisan gamer in his beret as he plays an obscure Welsh-language art-house experimental game that muses on the notion of grief and ontology, and not yourÂ mainstream gaming. No, not that at all. I just want the first time I play the incredible game to be as incredible as possible, and I know that the PC version will be a big step up, even from the incredible application of six-year-old tech on display in the PS5 version. The PC version will be designed to use day-old tech, pushed to work with the most recent graphics card and RAM you’ve been able to cobble together, and heck, it might even run at over 30 FPS.

But I’m not even driven by the tech. I just…like playing games on PC. It’s the machine I played games on as a teenager, and the machine that gave me a career writing forÂ PC Gamer and foundingÂ Rock Paper Shotgun. I love my PC. I like playing games at my desk, on my ultra-wide monitor, whether I’m using mouse/keyboard or a console controller. I get curling up on the couch and enjoying games that way, but there’s something about the intimacy of the screen being two feet from my face, not the other side of the room, that draws me further in. There are fewer distractions in my teeny office, carved into messy shape over years of gaming and working. And that’s another thing! It’s a far safer way to play a game like GTA 6 when there’s a 12-year-old in my house who cannot comprehend why I might not want him watching, let alone playing. A 12-year-old who wants to be camped in the same room as my PS5, playingÂ Minecraft on his Switch while on the phone to the other kids in the same realm. That’s no place for some 18+ gaming entertainment.

So what should I do? I still don’t know. My instinct is that I’m going to give in, fork out the Â£70 ($92) for a copy, and then be really annoyed with myself whenever the PC version does come out. I’ll have only been able to play the PS5 version in fits and starts, given the availability of the living-room TV and the appropriateness of who else is in the room, or I may sacrifice any notion of sleep and play the game nocturnally, frustratedly squinting to read the inevitably tiny text on the more distant television, knowing that it just won’t be the same to play it over again. But if I don’t, obviously everything that’s still a surprise will have long been spoiled for me by the time I play, and I’ll be missing out on the excited conversations of friends and colleagues who will be sharing amazing moments and crucial discoveries.

Bigger than that, I’ll not be part of the cultural zeitgeist, this enormous moment of shared entertainment that will beÂ everywhere, referenced inÂ everything, and by all accounts, utterly, stunningly good. And that sucks. But [wrinkled nose, sulky tone] I want to play to play it on PC. I just wanna. It’s not fair. I’m completely stuck about what to do.

Is Season 30 of The Voice making me a little bit country?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spoiler alert! This story discusses the Live Shows' Y2K Week on The Voice Season 30, which aired November 16. Episodes are available to stream the day after they air with a Peacock subscription.

The Voice Live Shows are in full swing on the 2026 TV schedule, and have been narrowing down Season 30’s incredible talent to the Top 10. In the latest episode of NBC’s long-running singing competition, they continued to pay tribute to the hits of the late ‘90s and early 2000s with Part 2 of Y2K Week with Team Riley and Team Kelly. From the Goo Goo Dolls hit “Iris” to The Chicks’ tune “Cowboy Take Me Away” to Keane’s indie rock track “Somewhere Only We Know,” there was a blend of musical genres that traveled all over the map and gave a glimpse into how challenging it will be to continue to cut singers, moving ever closer to the winning coach and star. I need to talk about the country music.

While veteran coach Kelly Clarkson knows firsthand what it takes to win, having taken the title four times in nine seasons, including during her first season as a coach, The Voice newbie Riley Green should not be deterred, as Season 30 is proving to be anyone’s game. Take it from this rock music fan, who’s quickly being won over by one of Team Riley’s country singers. Sure, Kelly has 14-year-old and 16-year-old powerhouse singers on her team – Brianna Cameron, who sang “Reflection” by Christina Aguilera, and Koumba Diallo, who sang the Alicia Key’s hit “Fallin’” – but it’s the teenager on Team Riley that is making the best case for crooning his way to the finals.

Country singer Joe Henley (not to be confused with Joe Hendry) is only 19 and had never played a gig before auditioning for The Voice, which only makes his journey on the show more impressive. After grabbing the attention of Kelly Clarkson and Riley Green during the Blind Auditions, making it through the Battle Rounds, and hands-down reclaiming his spot on Team Riley for Cut Week, he took on Lee Ann Womack’s “I Hope You Dance.”

It's one of those country tracks that has crossed over into the mainstream, with deeply emotional lyrics that I’ve personally connected with and that always pull on my heartstrings when I hear it. It was an unexpected choice to hear the #1 hit covered by a male, but Joe crushed it, reinforcing the possibility that he really could win it all in Season 30.

For a rock girlie to be saying that is a big deal! Just saying!

Sure, Team Adam and Team Kelly have the numbers advantage, with three singers still left on each of their teams while the other coaches only have two. I can’t believe I’m still on the country train, but I actually think that Team has a very good chance of winning in his first season, whether that’s with Joe Henley or the duo Ferryn & Brinkley. He’s proven to have an excellent ear for talent and has given great advice and guidance to his team as their performances have only gotten stronger.

While we already know the competition series will be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity, we won’t learn who will take it all in Season 30, and if that could be country singer Joe Henley, until December. So, be sure to keep tuning in to NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET until then.

Vice City International Airport is on the west side of Vice-Dale County. It's easy to spot with its two giant landing strips in a wedge shape on the southwest side of the city.

The GTA 6 airport, Vice City International, has a huge footprint on the map. You really can't miss it once you get into the city and start wandering around. There are two main runways that both have commercial jets parked in them at all times which you can sneak your way onto and fly off with if you throw it in reverse before those tarmac support vehicles get under your wheels.

Other than tons of jets, there aren't really a lot of map icons for specific activities at VCIA. It's a big campus, so there's lots of exploring, but not a very structured to-do list. After running off with jets and maintenance vehicles, you can also break into a ton of ATMs at the central terminal part of the airport.
